title: SOC 2 Automation Platform: Top Picks Compared (2026)
summary: SOC 2 automation platform options range from built-in connectors to workflow tools. You'll understand which approach best fits your audit needs.
body_markdown:
## SOC 2 requirements for workflow automation


Once the perimeter is drawn, any workflow tool that moves customer data across it is inside the audit, and it has to meet the same controls as everything else.


When an automation runs under a shared service account, writes customer records to a place nobody reviews, and leaves no log of who changed the flow, your auditor finds it, and the finding lands on you, not on the compliance platform.


Activepieces is not a SOC 2 compliance platform, but a team automating evidence reminders or access reviews with it can check the table below line by line: its SOC 2 programme (in progress, with the penetration test summary, DPA and sub-processor list available on request), SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs and self-hosting, each with the evidence to request.


Treat it as a checklist for any automation vendor, not only this one.


Requirement What Activepieces has Evidence to request


SOC 2 Type II In progress; pen test summary and DPA on request The report itself


SSO Supported Identity provider setup documentation


SCIM Supported Deprovisioning behavior on user removal


Custom RBAC Supported The permission model, per role


Audit logs Available What events are recorded and how to export them


EU or US cloud Managed cloud in either region Region confirmation for your account


Self-host and air-gap Supported Deployment documentation


Nothing here confirms which of the four Cloud plans (Free, Plus, Team or Ultimate) includes each of these seven rows, so get that mapping, along with the security documents, through[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) .


### How Activepieces meets each requirement


With SSO and SCIM, your identity provider grants and revokes access, so a departed engineer's flows stop running under their name. Custom RBAC limits who can edit a flow that touches production data. Audit logs give the auditor a record of changes.


Because Activepieces' SOC 2 programme is in progress, there is no SOC 2 report to inherit yet; the penetration test summary, DPA and sub-processor list are available on request.


Do not expect Activepieces to replace a compliance platform: of the seven rows in the table, the SOC 2 row is still in progress and would cover the vendor's own operation, not your controls, and the other six are capabilities you still have to configure and evidence yourself, which means you're building your own compliance platform.


A compliance platform collects evidence and tracks controls. A workflow tool is one more system whose controls must produce evidence. Buy it as you would any vendor in scope.


If your team can't send data to a third-party cloud, you can self-host, including air-gapped, so data stays in its own environment.


The core is MIT-licensed, so your security reviewer can clone the public repository at github.com/activepieces/activepieces, trace the queue and worker architecture, and load-test a self-hosted or air-gapped deployment before anything is signed, instead of relying on a vendor's description.


The LICENSE file in that repository shows exactly where the MIT core ends: the` packages/ee/` directories sit under a separate commercial licence. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production. The audit burden for that infrastructure then becomes yours.
